title: Split headline reveal
sub: Headline lines rise out of a mask
html:
Design that
moves people,
not pixels.
prompt: Build a hero headline that reveals line by line. Split the h1 into one block per visual line and wrap each line's text in a span inside an overflow: hidden wrapper (add a few px of bottom padding so descenders are not clipped). Start each span at transform: translateY(110%) and animate to none, so the text appears to rise out of a mask. Stagger the lines by 120ms using a CSS custom property per line (animation-delay: calc(var(--i) * 120ms)). Use a critically damped spring easing, for example a linear() curve that settles in about 700ms, or cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1) over 800ms. Fade the subcopy and CTA in after the last line, about 300ms later. Trigger it on page load or when the hero enters the viewport with an IntersectionObserver. Animate only transform and opacity. Keep the real text in the DOM and give the h1 an aria-label if you split by JS. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Blur-in words
sub: Each word sharpens in, one by one
html: Work that feels effortless
prompt: Build a hero headline where each word fades in from a blur. Split the h1 into word spans (display: inline-block, keep a normal space between them) and animate each from opacity: 0; filter: blur(10px); transform: translateY(6px) to opacity: 1; filter: blur(0); transform: none over about 700ms with cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1). Stagger each word by 70-140ms using a --i custom property in animation-delay. Fade the subcopy and button after the final word. Run it on load or when the hero scrolls into view with an IntersectionObserver, then remove will-change. Keep blur radius under 12px and only blur short headline text, never full-screen layers. Keep the original text readable to screen readers (aria-label on the h1 if split by script). Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Product float
sub: App mockup floats over a soft shadow
html: Your day, organized
prompt: Build a hero with a product mockup that floats gently. Put the mockup (an app screenshot in a rounded device frame with a hairline border and a soft layered shadow) on one side of a two-column hero. Animate the frame with a 4-5s ease-in-out infinite loop moving translateY between about +5px and -7px with a tiny rotate of +/-1deg, animating only transform. Add a separate blurred ellipse under it as the shadow and animate it the opposite way: scaleX shrinks and opacity drops while the mockup is high, grows back when it is low. Use filter: blur only on that small static ellipse. Add a subtle pointer parallax by translating the mockup a few px toward the cursor on pointermove, with a spring-like transition. Stack the columns on mobile. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Tilted screen settles
sub: Tilted app shot rotates flat on scroll
html: Your whole team, one screen
prompt: Build a hero where a 3D-tilted app screenshot settles flat as the visitor scrolls. Make the hero section tall (about 200vh) with a position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100vh inner stage so the screenshot stays on screen while scroll progress runs. Put the screenshot in a wrapper with perspective: 1200px and set transform-origin: 50% 0 on the image. Compute progress = clamp(scrollY relative to the hero / (heroHeight - viewportHeight), 0, 1) in a passive scroll listener (or animation-timeline: view() where supported) and apply transform: rotateX(calc(42deg * (1 - progress))) scale(calc(.9 + .1 * progress)). Animate only transform. Give the frame a hairline border and layered shadow. Use requestAnimationFrame to batch writes. For prefers-reduced-motion, render the screenshot flat with no scroll link. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Video hero with scrim
sub: Moving plate, scrim, headline on top
html: See it in motion
prompt: Build a full-bleed video hero with a readability scrim. Put a muted, autoplaying, looping, playsinline <video> (with a poster image) absolutely behind the content with object-fit: cover. Layer a scrim above it: a linear-gradient from rgba(0,0,0,.65) at the bottom to rgba(0,0,0,.1) at the top so white headline text keeps at least 4.5:1 contrast on any frame. Place the headline, one line of subcopy and a primary button bottom-left over the scrim. Add a thin progress line at the bottom that scales from 0 to 1 over the clip length (transform: scaleX). Add a pause/play button for accessibility, pause the video when the hero leaves the viewport (IntersectionObserver) and swap to the poster under prefers-reduced-motion. Keep the video under 3 MB for the web, with a webm and mp4 source. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Gradient mesh drift
sub: Soft blue blobs drift behind the text
html:
Calm, clear,
yours.
prompt: Build a hero background made of drifting soft gradient blobs. Absolutely position 3-4 circular elements behind the headline, each filled with a radial-gradient from a translucent brand color to fully transparent at about 68% (this gives the soft mesh look with no filter: blur). Use two or three tints of your accent color plus one very light tint on a white page. Animate each blob with its own transform keyframes (translate plus a little scale), 8-12 seconds, ease-in-out, infinite alternate, with different durations so the pattern never visibly repeats. Animate transform only. Put the headline and CTA above with position: relative and keep text contrast above 4.5:1 against the lightest and darkest blob positions. Use overflow: hidden on the hero, set pointer-events: none on the blobs, and stop the animation under prefers-reduced-motion. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Typewriter headline
sub: Last word types, deletes, cycles
html: Software built for
prompt:
Build a hero headline whose last word types and deletes in a loop. Markup:

Software built for designers, founders, creators and everyone

. In JS keep an array of words, type the current word one character at a time (80-100ms per character), hold it for about 1.3s, delete it faster (40ms per character), pause 350ms, then move to the next word. Use a self-scheduling setTimeout chain, not setInterval, and stop it when the tab is hidden or the hero is offscreen. Render the caret as a ::after pseudo-element (2px wide, accent color) that blinks with animation: blink 1s steps(1) infinite. Reserve the line height with min-height so the layout never jumps. Under prefers-reduced-motion show the first word statically. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Rotating word slot
sub: One word rolls like a slot reel
html:
Launch your
appsitestorebrandapp today.
prompt: Build a hero headline with one word that rolls vertically like a slot reel. Wrap the changing word in an inline-block "slot" with height: 1.2em; overflow: hidden and a fixed width equal to the longest word so the sentence does not reflow. Inside, stack the words in a column (each exactly 1.2em tall) and repeat the first word at the end. Animate the column with translateY in steps of -100%/N (N = word count including the repeat): hold each word about 2s, then roll to the next in 500-600ms with cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1). After the last roll the repeated first word makes the loop seamless. Optionally add a light accent-colored pill behind the slot. Use aria-label with the full sentence on the h1 and aria-hidden on the reel. Under prefers-reduced-motion show only the first word. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Hero with logo strip
sub: Logos scroll endlessly under the CTA
html: Ship faster with Flowly
prompt: Build a hero with a trusted-by logo marquee along its bottom edge. Put the headline and CTA above, and below them a full-width strip with a small "Trusted by" label and a row of customer logos (SVG, single color, grey-blue at about 60% strength). Make the track an inline flex row with width: max-content that contains the logo set twice, and animate transform: translateX(0) to translateX(-50%) with linear timing, 25-40s infinite, so the loop is seamless. Fade the edges with mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, #000 12%, #000 88%, transparent). Pause on hover and on focus-within (animation-play-state: paused). Give the logos alt text and mark the duplicate set aria-hidden. Under prefers-reduced-motion stop the animation and let the row wrap or scroll horizontally. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Bento assemble
sub: Tiles fly in and lock into a grid
html:
One place
for it all
prompt: Build a bento-grid hero where the tiles fly in and lock into place around the headline. Use CSS grid (grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr), 3 rows, 8px gap) with a few tiles spanning two rows or columns and the headline tile near the center; mix tile types (a gradient accent tile, a donut, a small bar chart, a list, a sparkline) with 16px radius and a hairline border. Give each tile a start offset in custom properties (--x, --y) pointing away from its slot and animate from opacity: 0; transform: translate(var(--x), var(--y)) scale(.6) to none with a spring easing (about 700ms), staggered 70-90ms per tile. Trigger it once when the hero enters the viewport with an IntersectionObserver; do not loop in production. Animate transform and opacity only. Collapse to two columns on mobile and show the final layout with no motion under prefers-reduced-motion. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Cursor spotlight
sub: A light follows the cursor over dots
html: Find your focus
prompt: Build a hero where a soft spotlight follows the cursor over a dotted grid. Layer two identical dot grids (background-image: radial-gradient dots on a 16px background-size): a base layer in a pale grey-blue and a top layer in your accent color with larger dots. Mask the top layer with mask-image: radial-gradient(circle 110px at var(--x) var(--y), #000, transparent) so only dots near the cursor light up, and add a faint accent radial-gradient glow at the same point. On pointermove set --x and --y on the hero from clientX/Y minus getBoundingClientRect, but ease toward the target inside a requestAnimationFrame loop (lerp 0.12-0.16) so the light trails smoothly. When the pointer is idle for 2-3s, drive the light along a slow Lissajous path so touch devices still see it. Keep text above with pointer-events: none on the effect layers. Under prefers-reduced-motion keep the light static at center. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Shrink into card
sub: Full-bleed hero scales into a card
html:
Wide open
spaces.
prompt: Build a hero where a full-bleed image scales down into a rounded card as the page scrolls. Make the hero container about 180vh tall with a position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100vh stage. Inside, a full-viewport image wrapper uses transform-origin: 50% 40%. Compute progress = clamp(scrolled / (heroHeight - viewportHeight), 0, 1) in a passive scroll listener (or animation-timeline: scroll() where supported) and set transform: scale(calc(1 - .3 * progress)) and border-radius: calc(24px * progress). Fade the headline out by progress .5 and reveal the next section's content underneath in the space the image frees up. Animate transform and opacity (radius changes are paint-only). Batch writes in requestAnimationFrame and fall back to the final card layout under prefers-reduced-motion. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Stacked screenshots
sub: Three app screens cycle to the front
html:
Every view,
in reach
prompt: Build a hero with three product screenshots fanned in a stack that takes turns coming to the front. Position the three frames absolutely in one container and drive their pose with a data-pos attribute (0 front, 1 and 2 behind): front is translate(0) rotate(0) scale(1); the second is translate(14%, -9%) rotate(6deg) scale(.94); the third is translate(-8%, 8%) rotate(-7deg) scale(.9). Transition transform with a slightly overshooting spring (linear() curve, about 600ms) and give z-index a short delay so the frame goes behind mid-flight. Every 2-3s rotate the data-pos values with a setTimeout chain, and pause on hover or when the hero is offscreen. Make each frame a button-less image with alt text; add previous/next controls and arrow-key support if you show it to users as a carousel. Under prefers-reduced-motion switch frames with a plain opacity crossfade. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Layered parallax
sub: Mountains and sun shift at depths
html: Above it all
prompt: Build a layered parallax hero from 4-6 stacked transparent PNG or SVG layers (sky, sun, far mountains, near mountains, foreground, headline). Absolutely position each layer slightly wider than the hero (left/right: -8%) so it can shift without exposing edges, and give each a depth value (0.1 for the sun up to 1.5 for the foreground and text). On pointermove normalize the cursor to -1..1 and, inside a requestAnimationFrame loop, ease the current offset toward the target (lerp 0.1) and set transform: translate3d(-x * depth * 12px, -y * depth * 4px, 0) on each layer. Also add a scroll component (translateY = scrollY * depth * 0.1). When there is no pointer for 2-3s, drive a gentle sine path so touch devices see depth. Animate only transform. Disable the parallax under prefers-reduced-motion, keep the layers stacked statically. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Zoom through
sub: Camera dives into a window, new scene
html:
Next stop:
everywhere.
Step inside
prompt: Build a hero where the camera zooms through a window into the next scene. Stack two layers: the first scene on top, with a framed window in its center that shows a preview of the second scene, and the second scene full-size underneath. Set transform-origin on the first scene to the center of that window and animate transform: scale() from 1 to the ratio (viewport width / window width), about 3x, with an ease-in-out curve like cubic-bezier(.6, 0, .3, 1) over 1.2-1.6s. Once the window fills the screen, fade the first scene out (opacity) to reveal the matching full-size second scene, then animate its headline in. Drive it from scroll (sticky stage, progress mapped to scale) or from a click on the window. Animate transform and opacity only, use will-change: transform briefly, and under prefers-reduced-motion cut straight to the second scene with a short crossfade. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Character stagger
sub: Letters drop in on springs, staggered
html:
Make it
move.
prompt: Build a hero headline where each letter drops in with a spring, staggered. Split the h1 into words (display: inline-block; white-space: nowrap so lines never break mid-word) and each word into letter spans with a --i index; keep the real text in an aria-label on the h1 and aria-hidden on the spans. Animate each letter from opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-120%) rotate(-8deg) to none using a slightly overshooting spring easing (a linear() curve with a 2% overshoot, about 650ms), delayed by calc(var(--i) * 45ms). Play it once when the hero enters the viewport (IntersectionObserver), then underline the headline with a gradient bar that scales from 0 to 1 on transform: scaleX and fade in the CTA after the last letter lands. Animate only transform and opacity. Under prefers-reduced-motion show the headline immediately. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Orbiting icons
sub: App icons orbit a central logo
prompt: Build a hero visual where app icons orbit around a central logo. Make a square container (aspect-ratio: 1) with the logo centered, and two concentric dashed ring elements (inset 0 and inset 24%). Each ring rotates with transform: rotate(360deg) linear infinite, 14s and 22s in opposite directions. Place each icon on its ring by wrapping it in an absolutely positioned layer rotated by its starting angle (transform: rotate(var(--a))) and positioning the icon at left: 50%; top: 0. Counter-rotate every icon with an animation of the same duration and direction that runs from rotate(-angle) to rotate(-angle - 360deg) so the icons stay upright. Give the icons a white rounded tile, hairline border and soft shadow, and add a slow expanding ring pulse behind the logo. Pause on hover if the icons are links. Use real links with accessible names, and stop the motion under prefers-reduced-motion. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

sub: Notification chips bob around a headline
html:
Everything,

prompt: Build a hero with small UI "chips" that float around the headline: a notification ("New signup - Maya R."), a metric ("+24% revenue"), a payment ("Paid $480") and a message count. Each chip is a pill with a hairline border, soft layered shadow and a small round icon tile in your accent tint, positioned absolutely near a corner of the hero (hide two of them under 640px). Animate each with a gentle bob: @keyframes bob { from { transform: translateY(4px) rotate(-1.2deg) } to { transform: translateY(-6px) rotate(1.2deg) } } with ease-in-out, alternate, infinite, a different duration per chip (3-4.2s) and a negative animation-delay so they are out of phase. Optionally let chips enter with a one-time spring scale-in staggered by 100ms and add a small pointer parallax. Mark the chips aria-hidden since they are decorative, keep the headline and CTA as the real content, and disable the bobbing under prefers-reduced-motion. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Split screen reveal
sub: Image panel wipes in beside the text
html:
Plan less.
Ship more.
prompt: Build a two-column split-screen hero: copy on the left, an image panel on the right that is revealed with a clip-path wipe. Start the panel at clip-path: inset(0 0 0 100% round 20px) and animate to inset(0 0 0 0 round 20px) over 900ms with cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1), so the image appears to slide in from the right edge. At the same time scale the image inside from 1.3 to 1 so it settles under the wipe, and fade and slide the left copy in from -12px with a 120ms delay. Trigger once on load or on entering the viewport with an IntersectionObserver. Animate clip-path and transform only. Stack to one column under 768px with the image on top. Give the image a descriptive alt, and under prefers-reduced-motion render the final state at once. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Image sequence scrub
sub: Product turns frame by frame on scroll
html:
Meet Orbit
Frame 01 / 12
prompt: Build a scroll-scrubbed product rotation hero (the Apple product-page technique). Use a tall section (about 300vh) with a position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100vh stage holding one (or an whose src you swap). Preload 60-120 sequential frames of the product turning, named frame-001.webp onward. In a passive scroll listener compute progress = clamp(scrollInSection / (sectionHeight - viewportHeight), 0, 1), map it to a frame index Math.min(count - 1, Math.floor(progress * count)), and when the index changes draw that frame inside requestAnimationFrame (canvas drawImage, cover-fit). Never animate between frames, the scroll position is the playhead. Show a small frame counter or progress ticks if useful. Set the first frame as the poster and load the rest progressively. Under prefers-reduced-motion show a single still frame. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Big number hero
sub: A huge stat counts up with its label

teams ship with Flowly

prompt: Build a hero built around one huge statistic that counts up. Show a small uppercase mono label ("Live this week"), the number at 56-96px, weight 800, letter-spacing -0.05em, font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums (so digits do not jitter), with a single accent gradient fill via background-clip: text, and a one-line description under it. In JS animate from 0 to the target over about 1.8s using requestAnimationFrame and an ease-out quartic (1 - (1 - t)^4), format with toLocaleString, and write textContent each frame. Start it when the hero is visible (IntersectionObserver), run it once, and reserve the final width (min-width in ch) so the layout never shifts. Fade a small delta chip ("+18% this month") in after the count lands. Put the real final value in an aria-label or visually hidden text so screen readers get the number, not the animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion render the final number. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Blueprint grid draw

prompt: Build a blueprint-style hero where grid lines draw themselves in, then the headline appears. Create the grid from absolutely positioned 1px elements (4 vertical, 3 horizontal, plus an inset frame) in a pale accent tint. Animate verticals with transform: scaleY(0) to 1 from transform-origin: 50% 0 and horizontals with scaleX(0) to 1 from 0 50%, 600-900ms with cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1), staggered by 100-120ms. (Do not animate width/height; scale a full-size line, or use stroke-dashoffset on SVG lines.) After the lines land, pop small crosshair markers on the intersections (scale 0 to 1) and fade the headline block in with a 12px upward settle and a white background so it stays readable over the lines. Optionally add mono spec labels. Run once when the hero enters the viewport. Mark the grid aria-hidden. Under prefers-reduced-motion render the finished grid. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Search hero

Find anything

For the demo behavior, cycle through 3-4 example queries: type each into the placeholder/field one character at a time (65-80ms), pause 250ms, then reveal 3 result rows with a staggered spring (opacity 0 and translateY(-8px) scale(.97) to none, 110ms apart, transform transition about 600ms with a critically damped linear() curve), hold 2-3s, hide them and clear the text, then continue with the next query. Style the field with a 1px accent-tinted border and a 3px soft accent ring, an icon on the left and a "/" keyboard hint on the right. Use a self-scheduling setTimeout chain, stop as soon as the real user focuses the input, and expose results as role="listbox" with aria-live="polite" when real. Under prefers-reduced-motion show one static query and results. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Chat demo hero

Style the user bubble in your accent gradient with white text, the assistant bubble as a light surface with a hairline border, and a small sparkle avatar. Use a self-scheduling setTimeout chain that stops when the hero is offscreen. Mark the thread role="log" aria-live="off" for the decorative loop. Under prefers-reduced-motion show the full finished conversation. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Card fan

prompt: Build a hero with a deck of cards that fans out from behind the main button. Position 5 thumbnail cards absolutely at the center above the CTA, stacked, all sharing transform-origin: 50% 130% (a point below the card so rotation sweeps like a hand of cards). The closed state is translate(0, 8px) rotate(0) scale(.86); the open state sets each card's rotation (-26, -13, 0, 13, 26deg), a horizontal offset (-34%, -17%, 0, 17%, 34%) and scale(1.1), using custom properties --a and --x so one rule handles every card. Transition transform with a slightly overshooting spring (a linear() curve, about 600ms), staggered 40-50ms outward from the middle card. Trigger it on button hover/focus-visible and on click for touch, and press the button to scale(.94) first. Cards are decorative, so mark the deck aria-hidden. Animate transform only, and under prefers-reduced-motion show the open fan without motion. Add a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that shows the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.
